02 · Insights

What H1told us

Seven patterns that only show up when the four reports are read side by side.

01+63%paid engagements, Q1 → Q2

Same budget, 63% more engagement

Paid spend moved +1.8% between quarters, while engagements rose +63% and blended cost per engagement fell 38%. Both units point to the same causes: campaign consolidation that started in 2025 and a boosting framework that puts money behind early high-performers instead of spreading it evenly.

Vision CPE
$0.039 → $0.021
Aesthetic CPE
$0.018 → $0.012

So whatKeep the framework. The gains came from where the money went, not from how much there was.

02290Kengagements from one video

One trend video can carry a quarter

The biggest single assets of H1 were clinic-shot, trend-native videos that worked on several platforms at once and kept working. Vision’s “I’m kinda busy” was the top performer on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok in Q2, with 290,278 engagements: 29% of all Vision paid engagements that quarter. Aesthetic’s “POV: Your esthetician fell” topped Instagram and Facebook in Q1 and topped Facebook again in Q2, 148,252 engagements across the half.

“I’m kinda busy”, Q2
290K engagements · 3 platforms
“POV: Your esthetician fell”, H1
148K engagements · 2 quarters

So whatTreat winners as a series, not a one-off: recut, re-boost and re-platform them, and brief the next one in the same format.

0327.34%Aesthetic LinkedIn ER in Q2

LinkedIn is the most reliable channel for professionals

Aesthetic’s organic LinkedIn engagements nearly doubled against H1 2025 (18.5K → 36.6K), and engagement rate reached 27.34% in Q2 against a 2% benchmark. Vision LinkedIn beat every goal in both quarters, and its CPM came down from $179.91 to $134.86. In both units, before-and-after clinical proof and named KOLs led.

Aesthetic LinkedIn ER, H1
25.0% vs 2% average
Vision LinkedIn CPM
−25% Q1 → Q2

So whatKeep feeding LinkedIn clinical proof (B&A carousels, KOL spotlights), and keep watching CPM, which is still the highest of any channel.

040.12%Facebook organic ER in Q2

Organic Meta now buys reach, not interaction

Aesthetic’s organic Facebook reach was up +78% on H1 2025, but organic engagements fell 69% and engagement rate slid from 0.28% to 0.12%, under the 0.90% benchmark. Instagram follows the same direction but still sits above its 0.70% benchmark. Interaction on Meta is now coming from paid: Aesthetic’s paid Facebook ER doubled to 71.84% in Q2.

FB organic ER
0.28% → 0.12%
FB paid ER
36.47% → 71.84%

So whatPlan Meta in two jobs: organic for visibility and frequency, boosting for engagement, with only proven posts boosted.

0533/34Vision KPIs met in H1

TikTok solved scale; interaction is the open question

TikTok reach grew in both units, but interaction did not keep pace. Aesthetic’s organic TikTok ER was 0.72% in Q2 against a 4% benchmark, and Vision TikTok missed one goal in H1: engagement rate finished at 39.04% against 45%. It is the only KPI out of 34 that Vision missed in the half. Both teams have prepared a Q3 shift back toward interaction.

Vision KPIs met, H1
33 of 34
Aesthetic organic TikTok ER
0.86% → 0.72%

So whatJudge TikTok in H2 by engagement rate and follows, and accept some reach as the trade-off.

06$19.96Accelerate CPL, Newport Beach

Video earns attention; static earns registrations

In Q1, video led Meta boosting on scale, ER and cost (44.2% ER on Facebook against 3.3% for static). Event campaigns showed the opposite: a new static drove 66% of Orlando registrations, statics carried 100% of NYC conversions, and one static delivered 57% of Newport Beach leads. Each Accelerate campaign cost less per registration than the one before.

Accelerate CPL
$31.70 → $28.97 → $19.96
Registrations, H1
315 from $13,475

So whatBrief formats by objective: video for boosting and awareness, people-led static for lead generation.

07#1share of voice in Q2

Q1’s white spaces turned into Q2 results

The Q1 competitive read named GLP-1 and “skin after weight loss” as an opening for triLIFT 2.0. In Q2, triLIFT 2.0 body content reached 63.68% ER on Instagram and 72.55% on Facebook, and the LinkedIn creative “Weight loss is changing” reached 38% ER. Over the same period Lumenis moved from fourth to first in aesthetics share of voice (15.1% → 26.7%) as Sofwave’s funded Q1 push faded.

Share of voice
#4 → #1
triLIFT 2.0 body, Q2
63–73% ER on Meta

So whatThe next openings are already named: science as storytelling, pro-aging, longevity, men’s aesthetics and hair loss.

  • Instagram is stabilizing with slight improvements in reach, engagements, and ER, early signs of recovery.
  • Facebook still reflects audience fatigue, but the pace of decline is slowing, indicating potential stabilization ahead.
  • LinkedIn delivered one of the strongest quarters, with significant growth in engagements and ER, driven by the new paid campaign structure.
  • TikTok improved reach efficiency significantly, driven mainly by a new campaign structure, though engagements and ER declined due to native reporting not including video engagements.
  • YouTube saw a natural stabilization in Q1 following the Q4 takeover (after a previously dormant period), maintaining performance significantly above Q1 last year despite the expected post-spike normalization.
  • X had no activity in Q1 last year; this quarter focused on testing and learning, with quote posts and KOL content performing best in Jan–Feb and driving a recovery in performance by March.

Competitive landscape · Q1

Sofwave emerged as the top-performing brand in the category the last Q, largely driven by a funded strategy and a boosted post promoting its March 16 virtual event on total body rejuvenation solutions. Sofwave is also investing in Google Ads, making it the only competitor with a clearly visible presence in this space.

GLP-1 Aesthetics

Create content designed for response, saves or shares, especially.
Educational AI Gap Open

Mensthetics
Strong whitespace for FoLix and Lumenis body-focused treatments to open a direct conversation with men.

Competitive landscape · Q1

The category leadership is still open. No One Owns “Clinical Expertise + Human + Innovation” Together. Competitors either dilute eye care, lack differentiation, or miss the human connection.

Reviewed: Envision by InMode, Alcon, EssilorLuxottica, Bausch + Lomb.

Learnings & opportunities · Q1

Platform roles
Facebook continues to drive scalable reach, while Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn lead on engagement, confirming a clearer channel role split.
Native formats drive performance uplift
Leaning into platform-specific formats (Reels, TikTok trends, LinkedIn document ads) significantly improved engagement rates.
Selective amplification is key to scale
Prioritizing high-performing content for paid support drove stronger engagement efficiency vs broad budget distribution.

Community: 96% positive across 1,318 mentions and 450 unique authors; top words were technology, eyes, treatment (Sprout Social, Q1 2026).

  • On Meta, reach held mostly flat QoQ but grew sharply YoY, a major visibility gain that put content in front of far more people. Engagements and ER kept compressing as reach outpaced interaction, reflecting the continued decline in organic consideration.

  • On X, engagements surged 2167% YoY and 31% QoQ, and engagement rate hit 6%, up 185% QoQ and now 3x the industry average.

  • On Facebook, campaign consolidation and a revised audience mix unlocked cheaper CPMs. Engagement was the standout, with ER more than tripling QoQ on the strength of trend-driven content. Reach dipped in line with lower spend.
  • On Instagram, our strongest engagement channel, better CPMs and stable spend delivered more reach, and engagements followed. ER nearly doubled an already strong Q1, fueled by trendy, platform-native content.
  • On LinkedIn, delivery costs recovered from the Q1 increase, and paid played a central role in expanding blended reach and engagements.
  • On TikTok, sharpening the content mix toward a clear B2C focus improved platform fit, driving stronger reach at better efficiency. ER remains the key optimization opportunity and will be our primary focus in Q3, with reach as a strategic trade-off.

Learnings & opportunities · Q2

Trend-driven content was the quarter’s engine
Trend-aligned, platform-native content drove the engagement surge across Meta, with ERs multiplying QoQ on both Facebook and Instagram.
The boosting framework proved itself
Prioritizing paid support behind early high-performers, rather than spreading budget evenly, delivered record engagement efficiency across channels.
LinkedIn CPM needs attention in Q3
Delivery costs are trending toward the $150 mark; optimizing CPM through audience and format refinement will be a priority to protect engagement efficiency on the platform.

How to read the numbers

  • Sources. The four quarterly social reports: Lumenis Aesthetic Q1 (April 2026) and Q2 (July 2026), Lumenis Vision Q1 (April 2026) and Q2 (July 2026). Quarter sections quote their findings verbatim; H1 totals and the “What H1 told us” section are new analysis.
  • Organic vs paid. Aesthetic reports organic (native platform) results and paid boosting separately. Vision reports paid media; its LinkedIn reach, engagements and ER are blended (paid + organic).
  • Engagement rate = engagements ÷ reach. YouTube uses engaged views ÷ views. H1 rates are recalculated from the half-year totals, so they are not an average of the two quarters.
  • Reach totals add channels and quarters together and are not de-duplicated; read them as volume of reach, not unique people.
  • Benchmarks are the industry averages used in the quarterly decks (organic and paid averages differ).
  • Community figures come from Sprout Social listening, which also captures conversation outside Lumenis channels.
